{{Short description|Type of projective plane}}

In [[geometry]], a '''Moufang plane''', named for [[Ruth Moufang]], is a type of [[projective plane]], more specifically a special type of [[translation plane]]. A translation plane is a projective plane that has a ''translation line'', that is, a line with the property that the group of automorphisms that fixes every point of the line [[Group action (mathematics)|acts]] transitively on the points of the plane not on the line.<ref>That is, the group acts transitively on the affine plane formed by removing this line and all its points from the projective plane.</ref> A translation plane is Moufang if every line of the plane is a translation line.<ref>{{harvnb|Hughes|Piper|1973|loc=p. 101}}</ref>

==Characterizations==
A Moufang plane can also be described as a projective plane in which the ''[[Desargues's_theorem#The_little_Desargues_theorem|little Desargues theorem]]'' holds.<ref>{{harvnb|Pickert|1975|loc=p. 186}}</ref> This theorem states that a restricted form of [[Desargues' theorem]] holds for every line in the plane.<ref>This restricted version states that if two triangles are perspective from a point on a given line, and two pairs of corresponding sides also meet on this line, then the third pair of corresponding sides meet on the line as well.</ref> 
For example, every [[Desarguesian plane]] is a Moufang plane.<ref>{{harvnb|Hughes|Piper|1973|loc=p. 153}}</ref>

In algebraic terms, a projective plane over any [[alternative division ring]] is a Moufang plane,<ref>{{harvnb|Hughes|Piper|1973|loc=p. 139}}</ref> and this gives a 1:1 correspondence between isomorphism classes of alternative division rings and of Moufang planes. 

As a consequence of the algebraic [[Artin–Zorn theorem]], that every finite alternative division ring is a field, every finite Moufang plane is Desarguesian, but some infinite Moufang planes are [[non-Desarguesian plane]]s. In particular, the [[Cayley plane]], an infinite Moufang projective plane over the [[octonion]]s, is one of these because the octonions do not form a division ring.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Weibel | first1=Charles |author-link=Charles Weibel | title=Survey of Non-Desarguesian Planes  | url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200710/ | year=2007 | journal= Notices of the AMS  | volume= 54 | issue=10 | pages=1294–1303}}</ref>

==Properties==
The following conditions on a projective plane ''P'' are equivalent:<ref>H. Klein [http://www.math.uni-kiel.de/geometrie/klein/math/geometry/moufang.html Moufang planes]</ref>
*''P'' is a Moufang plane.
*The group of automorphisms fixing all points of any given line acts transitively on the points not on the line. 
*Some  ternary ring of the plane is an alternative division ring. 
*''P'' is isomorphic to the projective plane over an alternative division ring.

Also, in a Moufang plane:
*The group of automorphisms acts transitively on quadrangles.<ref>{{harvnb|Stevenson|1972|loc=p. 392}} Stevenson refers to Moufang planes as ''alternative planes''.</ref><ref>If transitive is replaced by sharply transitive, the plane is pappian.</ref>
*Any two [[ternary ring]]s of the plane are isomorphic.
